label: UniFi Dream Machine Special Edition
description: Ubiquiti UDM-SE - 10G cloud gateway with NVR: 8x 1GbE RJ45 LAN (2 PoE+, 6 PoE, 180W), 1x 2.5GbE RJ45 WAN, 2x 10G SFP+.

poe.note: 180 W, from the tech-spec table row "PoE Budget = 180W" (with "PoE = 15.4W", "PoE+ = 30W", "Voltage Range PoE Mode = PoE: 44-57V / PoE+: 50-57V"), read 2026-11-19: https://techspecs.ui.com/unifi/cloud-gateways/udm-se . The same box's datasheet, https://dl.ui.com/ds/udm_se_ds.pdf (200, 358,669 B, text layer), prints the placement and per-port maxima but not the aggregate - "PoE interface (6) PoE (Pair A 1, 2+; 3, 6-) / (2) PoE+" and "Max. PoE wattage per port by PSE PoE: 15.4W / PoE+: 30W" - which is what the two PoE+ and six PoE poeOutClass values on ports 1-8 already follow. 8 ports at their class maxima is 152.4 W, inside the 180 W budget. The aggregate exists on the vendor page only; the datasheet is cited here so the placement is not read off the same table as the total.

notes:
Power: none of these copper ports accepts PoE. Vendor page https://techspecs.ui.com/unifi/cloud-gateways/udm-se (HTTP 200, 682,320 B, read 2026-11-19, server-rendered tech-spec table) says "Power Method = (1) Universal AC input, 100-240V AC, 4.4A Max., 50/60 Hz (1) USP-RPS DC input, 52V DC, 3.94A"; a box fed from mains, a USB-C supply or a DC jack has no PoE-PD front end, so WAN now declare poeIn: false. Without that declaration the engine's isPoePd() match on "unifi" gave each silent copper port a 12.95 W 802.3af draw - the defect PR #2118 and PR #2121 fixed across the UXG family (refs #130).

**LAN bank (layer 2), read 2026-11-21.** Both vendor surfaces print the same three rows: `MAC Address Table Size = 4,000`, `LACP Port Aggregation = True` with the note "GbE RJ45 ports 1-8", and `VLAN/Subnet-based Traffic Segmentation = True`, beside `1 GbE RJ45 = 8` and `2.5 GbE RJ45 = 1` (the WAN port) - https://techspecs.ui.com/unifi/cloud-gateways/udm-se (HTTP 200, 682,320 B), and the storefront's own payload repeats each row at https://store.ui.com/us/en/products/udm-se (HTTP 200, 602,395 B). A 4,000-entry MAC table is a bridge forwarding database, and a LAG over the eight 1G sockets cannot be built from routed ports, so Port 1-Port 8 forward at layer 2 and the row declares `l2-forward` (MAC learning + flooding only; VLAN, LAG and STP ride on it). Measured on the pre-change spec: hosts on Port 1 and Port 2 in 192.168.1.0/24 could not resolve each other's ARP, and `switchport access vlan 10` answered "cannot switch frames: it has no l2-forward capability". `no switchport` still makes a LAN port routed; the WAN port keeps its address. The two 10G SFP+ cages keep their addresses as well.

WAN/LAN separation, read 2026-11-21. Ubiquiti's controller device database numbers the sockets and names the uplink: https://static.ui.com/fingerprint/ui/public.json (HTTP 200, 832,585 B, `devices` entry with `sku` = UDM-SE) prints `ports` = {"eth0": "LAN", "eth1": "LAN", "eth2": "LAN", "eth3": "LAN", "eth4": "LAN", "eth5": "LAN", "eth6": "LAN", "eth7": "LAN", "eth8": "WAN", "eth9": "WAN2", "eth10": "LAN", "plus": [10, 11], "standard": 9} with `numberOfPorts` 11 - nine RJ45 sockets, the ninth the uplink, then the two 10G cages. The product page repeats the split in words: "Default WAN Ports (1) 10G SFP+ / (1) 2.5 GbE RJ45", beside "1 GbE RJ45 = 8 (1G/100M/10M)", "2.5 GbE RJ45 = 1 (2.5G/1G/100M/10M)" and "MAC Address Table Size = 4,000" at https://techspecs.ui.com/unifi/cloud-gateways/udm-se (HTTP 200, 682,320 B, read 2026-11-21). `role` is the field `engine/device.js` `ownsIpOn` reads ("WAN and LAN are separate L3 surfaces ... role separation outranks the VLAN shortcut"), and it fires only when BOTH sides carry one, so a LAN bank with no role leaves the invariant this repo already asserts for the RT-AX89X (test/port-roles.test.js, "the WAN port does not answer the LAN address") silently false: with 192.168.1.1/24 on Port 1, `ownsIpOn(WAN, '192.168.1.1')` returned the LAN interface, i.e. a host cabled to WAN inside that subnet was answered by the LAN gateway. WAN now declares role "wan" and Port 1 through Port 8 "lan"; measured after the change, WAN no longer owns the LAN address, Port 2 still reaches the address held on Port 1 (the bank still answers bank-wide), and WAN still answers an address of its own. **The two SFP+ cages, read 2026-11-21.** The previous sentence in this note said the cages stay role-less because "the datasheet prints one LAN and one WAN cage without numbering them". That is true of the datasheet and false of the controller: `https://static.ui.com/fingerprint/ui/public.json` (HTTP 200, 832,585 B, `devices` entry with `sku` = UDM-SE) numbers every socket of this chassis and both counts close - `numberOfPorts` 11 = `standard` 9 + the two entries in `plus` [10, 11], and `linkNegotiation` puts `eth9` at `portIdx` 10 (10000/1000 FDX) and `eth10` at `portIdx` 11 (10000/1000 FDX), while the same map names `eth9` "WAN2" and `eth10` "LAN". Nine RJ45 positions (1-9) plus two cage positions (10-11) is the whole box, so the cages are positions 10 and 11, and position 10 - the first SFP+ - is the default second WAN. The tech-spec page agrees in words: "Default WAN Ports (1) 10G SFP+ (1) 2.5 GbE RJ45", "10G SFP+ 2 (10G/1G)" (https://techspecs.ui.com/unifi/cloud-gateways/udm-se, HTTP 200, 682,320 B, read 2026-11-21). `SFP+ 1` therefore declares `role` "wan" and `SFP+ 2` "lan", both with `dualRole` ["wan","lan"] because UniFi reassigns these cages and the vendor's own "Max. WAN Port Count 8" is a ceiling, not a wiring fact. Measured after the change: the WAN cage no longer answers an address held on Port 1, the LAN cage still does, and a host on the WAN cage in the LAN subnet gets no reply. `udw.json` keeps its cages role-less on purpose - there the same database prints `standard` 19 beside `plus` [17, 20] on 20 sockets, which is 21 positions for a 20-port box, so its positions do not close and its cage order cannot be placed. Gate: test/ubiquiti-wan-lan-role-separation.test.js.
